tools.name: get_workspace_snapshot
tools.description: Request a fresh Workspace snapshot from the connected browser. Call this first when you need current dashboard state, dashboard identifiers across the workspace, or skill identifiers. The snapshot is intentionally compact: use list_available_widgets, get_widget_schema, and manage_dashboard for deeper follow-up inspection. dashboard_composition exposes deterministic tabs, layout coordinates, and groups for the current dashboard.

tools.name: list_available_widgets
tools.description: List widgets available to the current Workspace session. Returns deterministic widget identities for later get_widget_schema and create_widget calls. Optional filters: origin matches the friendly catalog label exactly; backend_id matches the backend UUID. Use backend_id only when you have a UUID from manage_backends; use origin when working from a snapshot. Both can be passed together for a stricter match. Without filters the entire catalog is returned, which can be hundreds of widgets — prefer a filter when you know the source. Generative-only note widgets such as rich_note are intentionally excluded; use add_generative_widget for those.

fields.description: Friendly catalog label (e.g. 'Options Activity Monitor'). Matches exactly.
Optional backend UUID returned by manage_backends.

tools.name: get_widget_schema
tools.description: Fetch the exact schema for one available widget. Returns deterministic params and UI inputs to use in subsequent create_widget / update_widget calls. Requires origin and widget_id from list_available_widgets — caller must select before calling. data_args_schema and ui_args_schema are closed JSON Schemas for the data_args and ui_args of create_widget and update_widget: a ui_args key or value they do not accept refuses the call, and a data_args value they do not accept is ignored with a warning. method is the widget's HTTP method, and each param's in says where its value goes in the widget's request: path, query, header or body. mcp_tool, when present, names the MCP tool of the widget's own backend that queries what the widget shows, and how its params fill the tool's arguments.

fields.description: Friendly catalog label from list_available_widgets.

tools.name: navigate_workspace
tools.description: Navigate the Workspace browser to an existing dashboard or inner tab. Requires operation from {dashboard, tab}. For dashboard, pass dashboard_id. For tab, pass tab_id. Resolve dashboard_id from current_dashboard_uuid before each write. Every successful command result includes session_context.current_dashboard_uuid (and current_tab_id) — reuse that from the previous response instead of calling get_workspace_snapshot again. Use get_workspace_snapshot only on the first call, or after a navigation step that may have invalidated the tracked context. Never match dashboards by name: duplicates with identical names are common. "This dashboard" means the current route; resolve via current_dashboard_uuid, not title. Omitting dashboard_id also targets the current route.

tools.name: manage_navigation_bar
tools.description: Create or mutate the Workspace navigation bar. Requires operation from {create, add_tabs, remove_tabs, rename_tabs}. For add_tabs, pass tabs_json as a JSON array of objects, for example [{"name":"AAPL Analysis"}]. The only tab object field for create/add/remove is name; do not send tab_id or tab_name. The tab_id is generated as the slug of name. Do not pass tabs_json as ["AAPL Analysis"]; string arrays are rejected. After add_tabs, navigate to the generated slug tab_id, e.g. AAPL Analysis -> aapl-analysis, before creating content for that tab. For rename_tabs, pass rename_map_json as a JSON object, for example {"old-tab-id":"New Name"}. Resolve dashboard_id from current_dashboard_uuid before each write. Every successful command result includes session_context.current_dashboard_uuid (and current_tab_id) — reuse that from the previous response instead of calling get_workspace_snapshot again. Use get_workspace_snapshot only on the first call, or after a navigation step that may have invalidated the tracked context. Never match dashboards by name: duplicates with identical names are common. "This dashboard" means the current route; resolve via current_dashboard_uuid, not title. Omitting dashboard_id also targets the current route. These tools operate on an existing dashboard only. They do not create dashboards. manage_navigation_bar manages the navigation_bar widget inside an existing dashboard. If the dashboard does not already have a navigation_bar widget, call create first. Its create operation creates or initializes navigation tabs on that dashboard; it does not create a dashboard. For create, add_tabs, and remove_tabs, tabs_json must be a JSON array of objects, for example [{"name":"AAPL Analysis"}]. Each object must use only the key name, not tab_id or tab_name. Do not pass a JSON array of strings such as ["AAPL Analysis"].

tools.name: create_widget
tools.description: Create one widget on a target dashboard. Requires origin and widget_id. Resolve dashboard_id from current_dashboard_uuid before each write. Every successful command result includes session_context.current_dashboard_uuid (and current_tab_id) — reuse that from the previous response instead of calling get_workspace_snapshot again. Use get_workspace_snapshot only on the first call, or after a navigation step that may have invalidated the tracked context. Never match dashboards by name: duplicates with identical names are common. "This dashboard" means the current route; resolve via current_dashboard_uuid, not title. Omitting dashboard_id also targets the current route. These tools operate on an existing dashboard only. They do not create dashboards. Use list_available_widgets and get_widget_schema first. For create_widget, pass origin as the exact catalog value returned by list_available_widgets. Pass data_args_json and ui_args_json as JSON object strings when config values are needed. Do not use this for rich_note; use add_generative_widget with widget_type='note'.

tools.name: update_widget
tools.description: Update one widget's config on a target dashboard. Prefer widget_uuid for read, update, and delete. widget_id is only a fallback when exactly one matching widget instance exists on the target dashboard. Never use a widget title or generic widget type such as rich_note as a layout identifier. Resolve dashboard_id from current_dashboard_uuid before each write. Every successful command result includes session_context.current_dashboard_uuid (and current_tab_id) — reuse that from the previous response instead of calling get_workspace_snapshot again. Use get_workspace_snapshot only on the first call, or after a navigation step that may have invalidated the tracked context. Never match dashboards by name: duplicates with identical names are common. "This dashboard" means the current route; resolve via current_dashboard_uuid, not title. Omitting dashboard_id also targets the current route. Visible placement is controlled by dashboard composition, not update_widget. Use manage_dashboard operation='read' or get_workspace_snapshot.dashboard_composition to inspect tabs and layout, then use update_widget_layout for x, y, w, h, and tab_id. The grid is 40 columns wide: full width is w=40, half width is w=20, one quarter is w=10. Typical minimums are about min_w=8 and min_h=4. If a navigation_bar is present it usually occupies y=0 with h=2, so the first content row usually starts at y=2.

tools.name: add_generative_widget
tools.description: Create a generative widget (note, table, chart, or html) with inline data. For add_generative_widget: note and html require data_json as the raw text or HTML content string; JSON string literals are also accepted. table requires data_json as a JSON array of objects. chart requires data_json as a JSON array of objects plus chart_params_json as a JSON object with chartType, xKey, and non-empty yKey. Use widget_type='note' for rich text notes such as rich_note. The response includes widget_uuid; use that UUID for layout changes. The inner_tab argument only places the new widget on an existing navigation tab; it does not create a tab. To put a generated widget on a new tab, first call manage_navigation_bar operation="add_tabs" with tabs_json such as [{"name":"AAPL Analysis"}], then navigate_workspace to the generated slug tab_id such as aapl-analysis, then call add_generative_widget without inner_tab so it lands on the active tab. Resolve dashboard_id from current_dashboard_uuid before each write. Every successful command result includes session_context.current_dashboard_uuid (and current_tab_id) — reuse that from the previous response instead of calling get_workspace_snapshot again. Use get_workspace_snapshot only on the first call, or after a navigation step that may have invalidated the tracked context. Never match dashboards by name: duplicates with identical names are common. "This dashboard" means the current route; resolve via current_dashboard_uuid, not title. tools.name: manage_backends
tools.description: Manage Workspace data backends (the connections that power widgets). Requires operation from {list, add, update, refresh, remove}. For list, returns each backend with id, name, url, status, and widget/app/agent counts. For add, requires name and url. Optional endpoint_headers_json is a JSON array of {"key", "value", "location"} where location is "headers" (default) or "query". validate_widgets defaults to true and surfaces a warning if widgets fail to load. For update, requires backend_id and at least one of name, url, or endpoint_headers_json. For refresh, requires backend_id; re-fetches widgets and templates from the backend URL. For remove, requires backend_id.

tools.name: manage_apps
tools.description: List, read, or instantiate apps from a Workspace data backend. Apps are full dashboard templates declared in the backend's apps.json: they bundle tabs, widget layouts, parameter groups, and suggested prompts. Instantiating one is the programmatic equivalent of clicking an app in the gallery. Requires operation from {list, read, instantiate} and backend_id. Use manage_backends operation='list' to discover backend_id values and app_count. For list, returns each app with name, template_id, description, tab_count, group_count, prompt_count, and allow_customization. For read, requires app_name (or template_id); returns the full app definition including tabs with layouts, parameter groups, and suggested prompts. For instantiate, requires app_name (or template_id); creates a fresh dashboard from the app template and returns its dashboard_id. Pass that dashboard_id to subsequent dashboard-targeting tools. activate defaults to true and routes the browser to the new dashboard.

App display name. Provide app_name or template_id for read/instantiate.

resources.description: Router for the Workspace app-builder resources. Read this first to find the right spec, guide, or example. Only for when the user has explicitly asked to build, review, debug, or extend a backend or app — not for composing dashboards from existing widgets.

resources.name: What Workspace Is
resources.description: Mental model of Workspace from the consumer side — Dashboards, Apps (templates), Widgets, Prompts, the AI Agent, and what is native vs. what your backend supplies.

resources.name: AI Agent Contract
resources.description: How Workspace's built-in AI Agent reads widget metadata and data, and the description / response-shape rules that make widgets agent-friendly.

resources.name: Backend Contract
resources.description: What a Workspace backend must expose over HTTP, language-agnostic.

resources.name: widgets.json Spec
resources.description: Top-level shape and critical fields for widgets.json, the widget metadata contract.

resources.name: apps.json Spec
resources.description: Served shape, tab/layout structure, and parameter group wiring for apps.json.

resources.name: Widget Types
resources.description: Catalog of widget type strings and a use-case-to-type quick selector.

resources.name: Widget Parameters
resources.description: Param types (text, number, boolean, date, endpoint), option sources, and the type-selection cheatsheet.

resources.name: Build an App
resources.description: End-to-end workflow for building a new Workspace app from scratch. Only for when the user has explicitly asked to build one.

resources.name: Review an App
resources.description: Structured review pass for an existing Workspace backend or app template.

resources.name: Debug an App
resources.description: Diagnostic order for apps that don't load, widgets that render empty, or sync that doesn't propagate.

resources.name: Convert an Existing Endpoint to a Widget
resources.description: Turn an existing HTTP endpoint into a Workspace widget — type selection, params, columns, validation.

resources.name: Minimal Backend (Generic HTTP)
resources.description: Framework-neutral picture of a Workspace backend — routes, response shapes, CORS, auth.

resources.name: Minimal Backend (Python + FastAPI)
resources.description: Recommended Python starter shape for a Workspace backend using FastAPI.

resources.name: Common Errors
resources.description: Curated list of the most common widgets.json, apps.json, layout, group, and endpoint failures with fixes.

resources.name: widgets.json JSON Schema
resources.description: The JSON Schema a backend's widgets.json is validated against for the signed-in user: the built-in types and the plugin types enabled for their organization, every key and value closed. Read from the user's Workspace session, so it needs the browser connected.

bridgeCommands.name: get_workspace_snapshot
bridgeCommands.description: Request a fresh Workspace snapshot from the connected browser. Call first when you need current dashboard state, dashboard identifiers, or skill identifiers. Use list_available_widgets, get_widget_schema, and manage_dashboard for deeper follow-up inspection.

bridgeCommands.name: list_available_widgets
bridgeCommands.description: List widgets available to the current Workspace session. Returns deterministic widget identities for later get_widget_schema and create_widget calls. origin matches the friendly catalog label exactly; backend_id is optional and must be an exact backend UUID from manage_backends. Without filters the entire catalog is returned (hundreds of widgets) — prefer a filter when you know the source. Generative-only note widgets like rich_note are excluded; use add_generative_widget for those.

fields.description: Friendly catalog label (e.g. 'Options Activity Monitor'). Matches exactly.
Optional backend UUID returned by manage_backends.

bridgeCommands.name: get_widget_schema
bridgeCommands.description: Fetch the exact schema for one available widget. Returns deterministic params and UI inputs to use in subsequent create_widget / update_widget calls. Requires origin and widget_id from list_available_widgets — caller must select before calling.

fields.description: Friendly catalog label from list_available_widgets.
Widget id from list_available_widgets.

bridgeCommands.name: get_params_options
bridgeCommands.description: Fetch parameter options for one or more widget input queries. Use only after get_widget_schema marks a param with requires_options_lookup=true.

fields.description: One entry per param to resolve. Use only after get_widget_schema marks the param with requires_options_lookup=true.
The origin of the widget.
The widget type id.
The name of the parameter to resolve.
The values that the lookup needs.

bridgeCommands.name: read_widget
bridgeCommands.description: Read one widget from the active dashboard. widget_uuid is the canonical instance identifier; widget_id is a fallback when only the type is known.

fields.description: Canonical instance identifier from a workspace snapshot. Preferred over widget_id.
Fallback widget type identifier when uuid is unknown.
Target dashboard UUID. Omit to target the current Workspace route.

bridgeCommands.name: add_widget_to_dashboard
bridgeCommands.description: Create one widget on a target dashboard. Requires origin and widget_id. Omit dashboard_id for the current dashboard. Creates on the current tab; navigate_workspace to the desired tab first for tab-scoped placement. Use list_available_widgets and get_widget_schema when you need catalog identities or config params. Do not use this for rich_note; use add_generative_widget with widget_type='note'.

fields.description: Friendly catalog label returned by list_available_widgets. Required.
Widget id from list_available_widgets. Required.
Target dashboard UUID. Omit to target the current Workspace route.
Widget config split into data_args (data inputs) and ui_args (UI inputs). Layout fields belong on update_dashboard_layout, not here.
The values of the widget's data parameters.
The values of the widget's interface settings.

bridgeCommands.name: update_widget_in_dashboard
bridgeCommands.description: Update one widget's config on a target dashboard. Handles 'update/set/change <param> to <value>' requests; the user may name a target widget by display name. Call only after identifying the target widget instances and confirming they expose the parameter being changed. Do not guess enum/dropdown values; call get_widget_schema and get_params_options when needed, then pass option values, not labels. For plain string values, preserve the user's literal casing unless schema/options require otherwise. Layout fields (x/y/w/h/grid_data/inner_tab/etc.) are rejected — use update_dashboard_layout for those.

fields.description: Canonical widget instance identifier from a workspace snapshot.
Fallback widget type identifier when uuid is unknown.
Target dashboard UUID. Omit to target the current Workspace route.
Widget config split into data_args (data inputs) and ui_args (UI inputs). Layout fields belong on update_dashboard_layout, not here.
The values of the widget's data parameters.
The values of the widget's interface settings.

bridgeCommands.name: delete_widget
bridgeCommands.description: Delete a Workspace widget from a dashboard. Provide widget_uuid (preferred) or widget_id. dashboard_id defaults to the current route.

fields.description: Canonical instance identifier from a workspace snapshot.
Fallback widget type identifier when uuid is unknown.
Target dashboard UUID. Omit to target the current Workspace route.

bridgeCommands.name: manage_dashboard
bridgeCommands.description: Create, read, or update one Workspace dashboard. create requires name. read uses current route if dashboard_id omitted. update requires dashboard_id and name.

fields.description: Operation to perform on the dashboard.
Dashboard UUID. Omit on read to target the current Workspace route. Required for update.
Dashboard display name. Required for create and update.
On create, whether to activate the new dashboard route. Defaults true.

bridgeCommands.name: update_dashboard_layout
bridgeCommands.description: Move or resize one widget on the active dashboard. Requires x/y/w/h grid coordinates. Optional min_w/min_h/max_w/max_h size constraints.

fields.description: Grid column position (0-based).
Grid row position (0-based).
Grid width. 40 = full row.
Grid height in rows.
Canonical widget instance identifier from a workspace snapshot.
Fallback widget type identifier when uuid is unknown.
Target dashboard UUID. Omit to target the current Workspace route.
Inner tab id to place the widget on. Omit to keep current tab.
Minimum width.
Minimum height.
Maximum width.
Maximum height.

bridgeCommands.name: manage_navigation_bar
bridgeCommands.description: Create or mutate the Workspace navigation bar (tabs). create / add_tabs / remove_tabs use tabs:[{name}]. rename_tabs uses rename_map:{oldId:newName}. tab_id is generated as the slug of name; navigate to that slug after add_tabs before placing content.

fields.description: Operation: create | add_tabs | remove_tabs | rename_tabs.
Dashboard UUID. Omit to target the current Workspace route.
Tab objects, e.g. [{name:'AAPL Analysis'}]. Required for create, add_tabs, remove_tabs. Do not pass tab_id; it is generated as the slug of name.
The name of the tab.
Map of {oldTabId: newName} for rename_tabs operation.

bridgeCommands.name: add_generative_widget
bridgeCommands.description: Create a generative widget (note or html) with inline content on a dashboard. The Workspace has no table or chart widget: draw a table or chart as an html widget (follow the `html-table` / `html-chart` skills).

fields.description: Generative widget kind: a markdown note or an HTML widget (tables and charts are HTML).
Target dashboard UUID. Omit to target the current Workspace route.
Widget content as a plain string: markdown for a note, an HTML document for html.
Widget display name.
Widget short description.
Existing inner tab id to place the widget on. Does NOT create a tab.

bridgeCommands.name: assign_tasks_to_agents
bridgeCommands.description: Assign tasks to configured external Workspace agents. task_requests items shaped like {id, description, assigned_holder_url, assigned_agent_id}.

fields.description: Tasks shaped like {id, description, assigned_holder_url, assigned_agent_id}.
The id of the task.
What the agent has to do.
The URL of the agent's holder.
The id of the agent.

bridgeCommands.name: navigate_workspace
bridgeCommands.description: Navigate the Workspace browser to an existing dashboard or inner tab. operation='dashboard' requires dashboard_id; operation='tab' requires tab_id.

fields.description: Navigation target: 'dashboard' (full route) or 'tab' (inner tab).
Dashboard UUID. Required when operation='dashboard'.
Tab id (slug-form, e.g. 'aapl-analysis'). Required when operation='tab'.

bridgeCommands.name: manage_backends
bridgeCommands.description: Manage Workspace data backends (the connections that power widgets). list / add / update / refresh / remove. add requires name and url. update/refresh/remove require backend_id.

fields.description: Operation to perform on backends.
Backend UUID. Required for update/refresh/remove.
Backend display name.
Backend base URL.
Endpoint headers. location is 'headers' (default) or 'query'.
The name of the header or of the query parameter.
The value that the backend's endpoints receive.
Whether it goes in the headers or in the query. The default is headers.
Whether to surface a warning if widgets fail to load. Defaults true on add.

bridgeCommands.name: manage_apps
bridgeCommands.description: List, read, or instantiate apps from a Workspace data backend. Requires backend_id. read/instantiate require app_name or template_id. instantiate creates a fresh dashboard from the app template.

fields.description: Operation: list | read | instantiate.
